text.p: The Tunisian parliament on Friday approved a 8.01 billion dinar ($8.01 billion) budget for the fiscal year 1997, up 10.8 percent from the current year budget.
The budget reduces income-tax rebates and increases borrowing to compensate for the loss of customs tax revenue since implementation of a 1995 free-trade zone accord with the European Union.
The government hopes to keep the net budget deficit at 640 million dinars, or three per cent of gross domestic product (GDP), from 575 million dinars in 1996 and three percent of GDP.
It plans to borrow a total 2.546 billion dinars in 1997, including 990 million dinars from abroad. Total borrowing in 1996 was 1.995 billion dinars.
The minimum corporate tax rate to encourage investments was raised to 15 percent from 10 percent.
Finance Minister Nouri Zorgati told the parliament the new taxation system will apply to 1996 incomes because of the need to boost government receipts as a consequence of losses from the customs tax.
Priority investments in agriculture, poor regions, environment and research will continue to be exempt from taxes, he said.

Although the accord with the EU is still awaiting ratification by some European countries' parliaments, Tunisia will implement the dismantling of customs barriers for the lists of goods as planned for the accord's second year. ($- 1 dinar)
